purpose: One reviewed set of shared-assurance component versions known to work together, with the digests that identify what those versions ship. Answers agent-ix/engineering-assurance#8.

accepted.note: Accepted by the named human, who directed an agent to transcribe the decision into this file. The agent did not make the decision. An agent may prepare this matrix and may not accept it.

gate.rule: Every component must classify as compatible before an enforcing migration begins.
gate.unknown_is_not_pass: A version this matrix has never seen is unknown, not compatible and not incompatible. Unknown never satisfies the gate.
gate.absent_is_not_pass: A component that could not be observed is unknown for the same reason.

components.name: quire-cli
components.provides: Static assurance export consumed by Quoin intake (quire-cli#74).

components.name: quoin
components.provides: Evidence transcription and retention, measurements, change-assurance records, proof attestations, intake, audit, and verification receipts (FR-068, FR-069).

incompatible_reasons.0.22.5: predates the `quoin change-assurance` surface; seal, intake, and receipt commands do not exist
incompatible_reasons.0.23.0: tagged but never published; its release run failed at the test leg on quoin#329, where an adapter accepted an inherited property name as a declared status

artifacts.note: Quoin's packaged receipt schema, retained beside the receipt it validates.

components.name: ix-flow
components.provides: Human decision events retained as an integrity-verified chain.

components.name: engineering-assurance
components.release: git tag v0.2.0 — source distribution only; npm publication is refused by design
components.provides: Shared verification semantics, the PGM-01 read-only compatibility mapping, and the accepted compatibility corpus gate (FR-008..FR-012).

fixtures.note: The accepted compatibility corpus is pinned as the `corpus` submodule and enforced by FR-011. Its chain artifacts are the cross-component fixtures this matrix claims pass.
fixtures.gitlink_is_the_pin: The corpus revision is whatever gitlink this repository records; FR-011 TC-078 asserts the checked-out commit equals it.

rollback.principle: Every pin here is a released artifact, so rolling back is installing the previous release. Nothing in this matrix requires a rebuild from source to undo.
rollback.quoin: Reinstall @agent-ix/quoin@0.22.5. The `change-assurance` commands disappear; retained records, attestations, and receipts are unaffected, because 0.23.x added a surface over existing contracts rather than changing the stored layout.
rollback.quire-cli: Reinstall @agent-ix/quire-cli@0.30.2. Exports produced by 0.31.0 remain readable; the provenance command is not present.
rollback.engineering-assurance: Check out the previous tag. There is none before v0.2.0, so rollback for this component means removing the dependency rather than downgrading it.
rollback.corpus: Move the `corpus` gitlink to the earlier commit and re-run the FR-011 gate. The corpus is content-addressed, so an earlier pin is a complete, self-verifying set.
rollback.irreversible: None of the above. No pin here migrates data, rewrites evidence, or changes a stored schema.

upgrade.order: quire-cli, then quoin, then this repository's tag, then the corpus gitlink. Each step is independently verifiable, and only the last one moves the gate.
upgrade.verification: After each step run `python3 scripts/check_compatibility_matrix.py`, which classifies what is installed against these pins and exits non-zero unless every component is compatible.
upgrade.what_does_not_change: No campaign repository is touched by an upgrade of these components. Migrations are agent-ix/engineering-assurance#10 and begin only after this matrix is accepted.

hosted_ci: Publication does not enable automatic hosted CI in any campaign repository. Every workflow in this campaign remains manual-dispatch only.

registry.rule: Every npm pin in this matrix resolves from the public npm registry. The internal npm.ix mirror MUST NOT appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc: it is unreachable from CI, and a pin that names it cannot be published or installed by anyone outside the network.
registry.mirror_is_not_an_oracle: npm.ix lags the public registry. Reading a version from it and concluding a release did not publish is a mistake that was made while preparing this matrix — quoin 0.23.1 was live on registry.npmjs.org while the mirror still reported 0.22.5. Verify a publish against the public registry.
